mechanism_claims.claim_text: Ctry2459 acts extracellularly as a virucidal anti-HCV peptide by disrupting HCV particle membrane integrity while leaving core/RNA comparatively less affected.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=16:Extracellular anti-HCV activity and viral inactivation of Ctry2459; xml:fig=2:Fig. 2

mechanism_claims.limitations: The local source supports virucidal membrane-integrity disruption for HCV particles, not a normalized MIC-style antibacterial mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Poor cellular uptake and endosomal retention limit intracellular Ctry2459 activity; lysosomotropic agents improve intracellular distribution and anti-HCV activity.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=17:Time-dependent anti-HCV activities and cellular localization; xml:sec=18:Effect of lysosomotropic agents; xml:fig=3:Fig. 3; xml:fig=4:Fig. 4

mechanism_claims.limitations: Chloroquine/Ca2+ are intervention evidence for uptake/endosomal escape, not standalone peptide modifications.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Histidine-rich Ctry2459-H2 and Ctry2459-H3 improve cellular uptake/endosomal escape and retain or enhance virucidal anti-HCV activity with lower toxicity in the reported assays.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=19:Design of histidine-rich peptides; xml:sec=20:Extracellular anti-HCV activities; xml:sec=21:Intracellular anti-HCV activities; xml:sec=22:Inhibition of the acidification of endosomes; xml:table=2; xml:fig=5:Fig. 5; xml:fig=6:Fig. 6; xml:fig=7:Fig. 7; xml:fig=8:Fig. 8

mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism is source-limited to HCV particle/cell-culture assays and endosomal-escape phenotype; no unsupported structural normalization or external supplement values are added.
